claim: Human decomposition cuts error roughly 20-fold (68x pooled) on extreme, high-uncertainty quantities (true value 7+ digits, large disagreement).
agent_test: Give the agent global vs decomposed estimates on extreme Fermi quantities; compare median error ratio at equal tokens.

claim: Decomposition does not help, and can hurt (about 458% higher median error in MA94), on familiar quantities with small uncertainty.
agent_test: Gate by an ADaPT-style trigger: try direct answers first, decompose when 3-5 direct samples disagree widely or confidence is low; compare to always-decompose at equal tokens.

claim: Gain is largest where the estimator knows least; prior confidence ranks with gain.
agent_test: Use model self-rated knowledge or sample spread as a trigger for decomposing.

claim: Decomposition fails when parts are not easier than the whole or part errors are positively correlated; compounding (1.2x1.2=1.44) and a shared wrong anchor multiply through.
agent_test: Inject a biased fact into one part; measure damage; test whether independent re-estimation of parts limits it.

claim: Self-chosen decompositions were not better than given ones in humans (small, non-significant); LLMs fine-tuned to find the decomposition produce rarely meaningful ones.
agent_test: Compare agent-written vs templated decompositions on same questions.

claim: Decomposition lowers stated confidence but overconfidence remains (global 28.0 vs decomposed 23.6 points over).
agent_test: Measure interval coverage with and without decomposition; do not assume decomposition fixes calibration.

claim: LLMs remain badly overconfident on Fermi questions (nominal 99% intervals cover about 65%); conformal recalibration fixes coverage.
agent_test: Apply conformal wrapper to agent intervals on a held-out Fermi set.

claim: LLMs stay off by orders of magnitude when they must find the decomposition and facts themselves (T5 question-only score about 0.01-0.04; GPT-4 fp_score 0.47-0.50).
agent_test: Score agent on Kalyan real Fermi set with fp_score, with and without retrieval.

claim: Executing a written program beats directly guessing the answer for a Fermi task (0.36 vs 0.18 with facts supplied).
agent_test: Let agent compute via code vs mental arithmetic at equal tokens.

claim: Prompt-only Fermi/event/time decomposition did not improve Brier for LLM forecasters on 100 ForecastBench questions (all adjusted p=.774); Bayesian-style prompts hurt (+.030). (Study 1: 38 prompts, 4 models, no retrieval; Fermi +0.008, event +0.007, time -0.008, all adjusted p .774.)
agent_test: Replicate with larger question set and an isolated decomposition arm at equal tokens.

claim: Subquestion decomposition with blind sub-forecasts improved Gemini 3 Pro Brier from 0.141 to 0.132 on 500 questions (94.4% of bootstraps); CIs overlap, one model, one set, and the decomposed arm also received extra GPT-5 research (not an equal-compute test). The gain sits in the calibration term (0.026 to 0.008) while refinement fell (0.091 to 0.083).
agent_test: Reproduce with blind sub-forecasting vs same-budget extra sampling.

claim: Evidence on LLM forecasting decomposition conflicts: blind sub-forecast (c01) helps slightly; plain prompt decomposition (b13) does not. Difference may be blindness to the parent question, tools and web research.
agent_test: Run three arms at equal tokens on one question set with retrieval: direct, extra research without structure, blind subquestions.

claim: Sub-question generation inside a retrieval pipeline is part of the strongest published LLM forecaster (Brier .179 vs crowd .149) but was never ablated; the whole retrieval stack is worth only about 0.02 Brier (no fine-tuning and no retrieval 0.206).
agent_test: Ablate sub-question queries in a replica retrieval pipeline.

claim: Models know the sub-answers but fail to compose them: compositionality gap about 40% for GPT-3 at all sizes, 42.9% ChatGPT, 23.0% GPT-4; self-ask narrows it.
agent_test: Measure agent gap: both one-hop correct yet two-hop wrong; test explicit recompose step.

claim: Confidence in sub-answers predicts compositional success (81.1% vs 42.6% by perplexity band).
agent_test: Gate decomposition recomposition on sub-answer confidence.

claim: Explicit decomposition helps most on long or compositional tasks and little on short ones (GSM8K 2-step L2M 74.53 vs CoT 76.68, 5+ steps 45.23 vs 39.07; SCAN 99.7 vs 16.2).
agent_test: Decompose only when estimated step count is at least 4; compare to always.

claim: Two-stage decompose-then-solve beats single-stage; a small model can decompose, but a weak solver cannot be rescued.
agent_test: Cheaper decomposer plus strong solver at equal cost.

claim: Factored decomposition (separate contexts) is more faithful but not more accurate than chain of thought; CoT 86.0 vs CoT-decomposition 85.6 vs factored 81.8 average (Radhakrishnan Table 4, corrected).
agent_test: Compare factored vs in-context decomposition accuracy and faithfulness at equal tokens.

claim: Decomposition yields testable probability laws; violations of Cond consistency correlate with Brier (0.92/0.87 on first dataset, 0.71/0.69 second), and low-cost consistency checks can patch forecasts. But the consistency-patching forecaster did not improve ground-truth Brier and did not generalise to held-out checks, so it is a monitor, not a fix.
agent_test: Compute P(A)P(B|A) vs P(A and B) gap on agent outputs; correlate with error.

claim: Forecaster training bundling comparison classes with other steps gave 6-12% Brier gains (year 1 10-11%, year 2 12%, year 3 6%, year 4 7%); decomposition not isolated, and the words do not appear in Chang 2016. A 2025 re-analysis finds the team and training effects shrink or flip after controlling extraneous variables.
agent_test: None; training study, not isolable.

claim: Tetlock's book is cited as the key work but no quantified decomposition effect was obtained.
agent_test: Locate the Mellers/Tetlock superforecaster decomposition data.

claim: Blind sub-forecasts (answered without the parent question or draft) beat in-context answers in the one nearby LLM test (CoVe FACTSCORE 63.7 vs 60.8); no test exists for numeric forecasts.
agent_test: Compare blind vs in-context sub-forecasts at equal tokens on a numeric forecasting set.

claim: Decompose-on-failure beats both always-decompose and never-decompose in agent tasks (ADaPT: ALFWorld 71.6 vs 43.3; WebShop plan-and-execute 17.0 vs ReAct 32.0 vs ADaPT 44.0).
agent_test: Use spread across direct samples as the failure proxy for forecasting and test it.

claim: Stepwise reasoning pays mainly on math and symbolic tasks (+14.2, +12.3, +6.9 points) and about +0.7 elsewhere; a numeric multiplicative structure is a plausible trigger for decomposition.
agent_test: Check whether question structure (numeric product of factors) predicts decomposition gain.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Instructed Fermi decomposition beats number-combining in human groups by a small margin (Study 2 d=0.26, CI -0.09 to 0.61, p=0.039); group use beats solo use (beta -0.24).
agent_test: Merge several independent decompositions by reasoning, not by averaging alone.

claim: Training studies of superforecasters do not isolate decomposition; Chang 2016 is silent on it, and the Mellers 2014 training and team effects weaken under re-analysis.
agent_test: Do not cite superforecaster training as evidence for O3.

claim: Consistency violations (Cond) correlate with Brier at the forecaster level (0.92/0.87 and 0.71/0.69) but are not shown to work as a per-question gate.
agent_test: Test the Cond gap per question as a trigger for resampling.
